concept_thesis: External support-frame acceleration can create corrective locomotion without an initial support-topology break: intact contacts redistribute load, one foot releases only after COM lag becomes unsustainable, a backward counterstep catches the relative fall, then a long catch-up step overruns into progressively shorter corrections and a displaced restack.

keys.name: STABLE_CARRY
keys.causal_role: Constant-velocity support frame carries the body with balanced two-foot load; no local locomotion key is earned by parent translation alone.

keys.name: ACCELERATION_JOIN
keys.causal_role: Support frame accelerates right faster than the root; unchanged contacts redistribute load toward the trailing/left foot and the torso counterleans.

keys.name: PEAK_INERTIAL_LAG
keys.causal_role: The platform continues gaining speed while both feet remain attached; COM lags deeper and trailing support load peaks without a topology change.

keys.name: RIGHT_RELEASE
keys.causal_role: The lighter right contact releases only after inertial lag has made the two-foot base insufficient; left support still moves with the accelerating frame.

keys.name: BACKSTEP_PROBE
keys.causal_role: Released right foot probes backward in platform space while the left foot remains the sole support owner; the root has not yet been rescued.

keys.name: BACKSTEP_CATCH
keys.causal_role: Backward right-foot catch widens the base behind the lagging COM and compresses the root; support transfer arrests the relative fall without stopping platform travel.

keys.name: CATCH_COMPRESSION
keys.causal_role: Right support absorbs the lag at maximum compression while the old left support unloads; platform motion continues, so the debt is not yet paid.

keys.name: LONG_CATCHUP_DRIVE
keys.causal_role: With acceleration spent into the catch, the planted right foot now drives a long catch-up surge relative to the still-moving platform; spacing spikes rather than resetting gait.

keys.name: FORWARD_PROBE
keys.causal_role: Long left-foot probe reaches ahead in the moving support frame while right support continues propulsion; root spacing remains larger than platform spacing.

keys.name: FORWARD_CATCH
keys.causal_role: Forward catch converts the catch-up surge into compression; torso counterlean begins while the previous support peels away.

keys.name: ROOT_OVERRUN
keys.causal_role: Residual self-propelled catch-up momentum carries the root beyond the first forward catch; upper body lags the renewed surge and the next probe overreaches.

keys.name: SHORT_CORRECTION_CATCH
keys.causal_role: Shorter right-foot catch pays the overrun with renewed compression; cadence contracts instead of mirroring the long catch-up step.

keys.name: SECONDARY_LAG_PEAK
keys.causal_role: Root motion nearly matches the platform while head and arms continue forward; the body has support but still owes secondary-motion recovery.

keys.name: SETTLE_PROBE
keys.causal_role: A modest left probe narrows the correction; root travel now approximately follows the platform instead of chasing it.

keys.name: DUAL_SUPPORT_SETTLE
keys.causal_role: Both contacts are restored with a slight right-side load bias; root spacing is now subordinate to support-frame travel.

keys.name: DISPLACED_RESTACK
keys.causal_role: The body restacks while remaining thirty-five pixels behind its original local platform address: acceleration debt is paid functionally, not erased by an idle reset.
